diagnosis.root_cause: The secondary FreeRADIUS server has a stale password record following the 2026-09-20 profile upgrade. Authentication succeeds through the primary but is rejected by the secondary, so MikroTik failover causes intermittent session drops and reconnections.
evidence: The subscriber is currently online and the ONU responds normally, so this is not an active ONU-offline condition.
RX power is approximately -21 dBm and TX power approximately +2.4 dBm, both within normal EPON ranges.

Seven days of optical telemetry are stable: RX variation is within the healthy noise range, TX variation is within the healthy noise range, distance remains constant at 228 m, and TX bias current remains healthy without a rising trend.
All observed peers on EPON0/2 are online with normal optical levels, and the OLT reports all eight PONs healthy.
OLT CPU, memory, temperature, uptime, and router heartbeat are normal, excluding OLT, PON-port, router, and broad infrastructure faults.
The subscriber has 13 sessions in 24 hours and an average duration of only 104 minutes versus the 11.9-hour network mean, confirming abnormal repeated reauthentication.
The RADIUS state explicitly reports a stale secondary password, authentication rejection on the secondary, and session starts correlating with primary acceptance and secondary rejection.
The VLAN walk shows the expected customer VLAN 1102, so provisioning VLAN 46 or customer VLAN misconfiguration is not implicated.

remediation.action: Synchronize the affected radcheck record from the primary to the secondary, verify the username, password, line ID, and profile attributes on both RADIUS servers, then test authentication through each server independently. Re-authenticate the subscriber after synchronization and audit other records changed during the same profile upgrade for replication lag. Add monitoring and alerting for RADIUS replication divergence; avoid routing this subscriber to the stale secondary until consistency is confirmed.

ground_truth.root_cause: A password change made during a profile upgrade on 20 September replicated to the primary FreeRADIUS but not the secondary. When the MikroTik fails over, the secondary rejects the customer; when the primary answers, authentication succeeds. The result is repeated disconnection and recovery with no physical cause.
expected_reasoning: Thirteen sessions in 24 hours against a 2-3 baseline, with a 104 minute mean against an 11.9 hour norm
RX has been flat at -21.0 dBm for seven days inside the noise floor, and TX, bias, voltage and distance are all stable
The live probe confirms the ONU is online and healthy, and peers on the port are normal
The OLT and router are healthy, so no shared infrastructure fault exists
With the optical layer conclusively clean, the cause must lie in authentication
The radcheck row on the primary is current, so a single-server check would find nothing wrong
Comparing both servers shows the secondary holds a stale row from before the 20 September profile change
Session outcomes correlate with which server answered rather than with any signal or time of day
The throughput series shows recurring zero windows that match the rejected attempts
Inconsistent state across replicated servers explains intermittency that no single query reveals

expected_escalation.review_reason: Master-slave replication between the FreeRADIUS pair is lagging; other customers changed since 20 September may be affected

distractors: The session pattern is identical to signal-related flapping
The primary RADIUS record is entirely correct, so a single-server check finds nothing
Self-recovering drops suggest an intermittent physical fault
Traffic alternates between normal and reduced days, which looks like usage variation
